reason: The storm requires reserve power, and the service panel has a matching essential-power slot.
expectation: The panel will select the charged reserve for essential power.

effect: Essential power is selected; the exterior well and fuel fab still need to be made safe.
reaction: The separate shutdown controls make the transition to reserve clear.
reason: The insulated water line corresponds to the panel's well isolation and drainage control.
expectation: The panel will isolate and drain the exterior well circuit.

effect: The exterior well line is isolated and drained before its heating switches off; the fuel fab still needs shutdown.
reaction: The confirmed drain sequence makes physical sense.
reason: The running fuel fab matches the panel's shutdown control and the storm warning to stop industrial loads.
expectation: The panel will shut down the fuel fab safely.

effect: The fuel fab completed cooldown and isolation, leaving the exterior circuits safe and completing the chapter.
reaction: The separate boil-off vents and confirmed shutdown make the storm response feel physically grounded.

mostWorthwhile.text: Draining the well line before switching off its trace heating was the most worthwhile action: the sequence explained how the equipment was protected during the outage.

leastWorthwhile.text: Selecting reserve power was clear but largely a matching exercise; the panel's named slot made the choice predictable.

surprise.text: The cold tanks retain some liquid while venting boil-off during the shutdown; stopping production does not simply preserve all the propellant.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt purposeless, though fitting whole system items into panel slots was an abstract way to represent operating their controls.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see the storm's consequences and how operations resume, particularly after learning that some propellant is lost to boil-off.
